what: rvc_service/rt_server.py (multi-session infer/rtrvc.py server) exercised with experiments/latency-sonnet/scripts/bot_client.py, real-time-paced WebSocket bots, against the live demo instance on VM209 (127.0.0.1:8093, loopback-only).

runs.label: 3 concurrent continuous-speech bots (bot-ru, bot-en, bot-ru2, staggered starts 0s/1s/2s)
runs.result: over capacity: each session's per-block processing rose to ~430-475ms (vs ~110ms solo) because 3 sessions round-robin one GPU via the shared lock; demand (3 calls per 0.3s window) exceeds supply (~1 call per 0.11-0.14s), so each session's asyncio.Queue(maxsize=4) filled and every session hit the 'overloaded' SessionError and stopped cleanly -- no crash, no corrupted audio, no queue growing unboundedly.
runs.audio_note: bot-ru's and bot-en's partial output from this run were overwritten on disk by the 2-session run below before being copied off the VM (same /tmp filenames) -- only bot-ru2's partial output survived, kept as the one example that a partial/overloaded session's already-served audio is still clean, not corrupted.

runs.label: 2 concurrent continuous-speech bots (bot-ru, bot-en, staggered starts 0s/1s)
runs.result: sustained indefinitely: both ran their full 20s input to completion (19.8s output each, no drops), per-block processing 144-228ms (RTF ~0.48-0.76 including lock-sharing overhead), well under the 300ms block budget.

reading: This GPU sustains about 2 simultaneous, fully continuous (no pauses) real-time speakers at block_s=0.3 with this shared-single-GPU-lock design; a 3rd pushes total demand over capacity. Real speech has pauses (unlike these scripted bots' back-to-back playback), so in practice more than 2 real human participants could likely coexist before hitting the same wall -- this number is a worst-case (100% duty cycle) floor, not a hard user-facing limit. The failure mode is exactly what the project's existing design principle calls for (LIVE_STATUS.md: overload ends the session explicitly rather than growing the queue indefinitely) -- no crash, no cross-session audio corruption, no server restart needed; the two survivors in the 3-bot run kept working normally throughout.
